covpp.coverage_planning.contour.coverage_pp_contour module

Contour Line-based Coverage Path Planning implementation.

class CoveragePathPlanner(cell: PCell, zmd: ZoneMapData)

Bases: CoveragePathPlannerBase

Coverage path planner using contour-following approach.

This planner generates spiral or contour-following paths by progressively shrinking the cell polygon or using distance transforms.

Planning Methods:

  • Polygon buffering: Iterative inward scaling

  • Distance transform: Skeleton-based path generation

  • Combination: Hybrid approach for complex shapes

Result:

Sets path_m and path_px attributes for the cell.

coverage_planning() → None

Execute contour-following coverage planning for the cell.

Result: self.path_px and self.path_m become a continuous contour sweep tailored to the zone cell.

calculate_path_by_poly_buffer() → None

Calculate coverage path by iteratively shrinking the cell polygon.

Uses polygon buffering to create concentric contours that form a spiral coverage pattern.

calculate_path_combinaiton() → None

Calculate the coverage path by distance transform and inscribed rectangle if available.

complete_path_by_rectangle(points: list, robot_r_px: int) → MyPath

Complete the path using the inscribed rectangle of the cell.

Steps: 1. Start from the inscribed rectangle and scale it down iteratively. 2. Rearrange and add rectangle points to the path. 3. Handle the center line if necessary (e.g., for odd-width rectangles). 4. Create the final path.

complete_path_by_distance_transform(points: list, c_map: ndarray, s_xy: ndarray, robot_r_px: int) → MyPath

Complete the path using distance transform method.

Steps: 1. Compute the distance transform of the cell map. 2. Iteratively find contours at increasing distances from the boundary. 3. Rearrange and add contour points to the path. 4. Handle any remaining area with a final contour extraction.

find_poly_by_dist(dist_transform: ndarray, dist: int, tolerance: int = 1) → list[Polygon]

Find polygons in the distance transform map that are close to the target distance.

rearrange_polys_by_area(polys: list[Polygon]) → list[Polygon]

Rearrange polygons by area in descending order.
